kept.claim: raw_html posts skip all sanitization, so HTML from the RSS feed or a scraped page (script tags, on* handlers, javascript: URLs) is stored in `cooked` and rendered verbatim on the forum and in the embed iframe.
kept.body: ## [ISSUE] `cook_method: raw_html` returns unsanitized third-party HTML as `cooked` (stored XSS) **Severity:** HIGH — raw_html posts skip all sanitization, so HTML from the RSS feed or a scraped page (script tags, on* handlers, javascript: URLs) is stored in `cooked` and rendered verbatim on the forum and in the embed iframe. ### The Problem ```ruby return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html] ``` For imported posts `cooked == raw`, and `raw` comes from: - `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` (`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35`): `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. This decodes entity-escaped HTML in the feed and passes it on with no filtering at all. - `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (`app/models/topic_embed.rb:48-50`): Readability keeps `a`/`img` with `href`/`src`, but it does not check URL schemes, so `` gets through. `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` only rewrites relative URLs. Nothing removes `
kept.evidence: post.rb:133 returns raw unchanged for raw_html. PostCreator:105 and ProcessPost store it as cooked with no PrettyText sanitization. poll_feed.rb:35 passes feed HTML through unfiltered. It is rendered via `raw post.cooked` in best.html.erb:19 and in the normal topic view. The Readability path strips script/on* but not javascript: hrefs.

kept.claim: The source URL is interpolated unescaped into an HTML attribute, so a feed link containing a single quote injects arbitrary attributes/markup into the raw_html post.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Unescaped `url` interpolated into `` in the imported-from footer **Severity:** MEDIUM — The source URL is interpolated unescaped into an HTML attribute, so a feed link containing a single quote injects arbitrary attributes/markup into the raw_html post. ### The Problem ```ruby contents << "\n
\n#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")}\n" ``` `url` is `i.link` / `i.id` from the feed (`poll_feed.rb:32-33`) or the `embed_url` query parameter (via `TopicRetriever`). The only check is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` on line 11. That regex is anchored at the start of the line only, and nothing constrains the characters after it. ### Theory / Proof A URL like `http://blog.example.com/x' onmouseover='alert(document.cookie)` passes the regex. It produces ``. Because the post is `raw_html` (Post#cook returns `raw`), this markup reaches `cooked` unchanged. Also note that Ruby's `^` matches at any line start, so a multi-line value passes as long as any line starts with `http`. ### What happens today vs. what will break With normal URLs this works. It breaks when a URL contains `'`, `<`, or a newline. The retriever path is the more dangerous one. `embed_url` comes from the `/embed/best` query string (`embed_controller.rb:15`), and the only gate is a Referer header that any client can set. `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` checks only the host, and Ruby's RFC 3986 `URI()` accepts `'` in paths and query strings. So an anonymous request with `embed_url=http:///post?a='onmouseover='alert(1)` is fetched by `import_remote` (most blogs return 200 when they see unknown query parameters) and then interpolated into this anchor. The result is stored XSS in a raw_html post that nobody on the forum wrote. ### Research Rails' `ERB::Util.html_escape` (`h`) and `CGI.escapeHTML` exist for this case. OWASP rule 2: attribute-escape untrusted data before putting it in an HTML attribute. ### Recommendation ```ruby return unless url =~ /\Ahttps?\:\/\// escaped = CGI.escapeHTML(url) contents << "\n
\n#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{escaped}")}\n" ```
kept.evidence: topic_embed.rb:13 interpolates url unescaped, and line 11 uses ^ instead of \A. On the retriever path, embed_url comes from the query string (embed_controller.rb:15). The Referer gate can be spoofed, invalid_host? checks only the host, and Ruby's URI accepts ' in path/query, so an anonymous user can inject attributes into the raw_html post.

kept.claim: absolutize_urls treats protocol-relative URLs (`//cdn.example.com/x.png`) as root-relative and rewrites them to `http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png`, breaking images and links.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Protocol-relative URLs are corrupted by `absolutize_urls`

**Severity:** MEDIUM — absolutize_urls treats protocol-relative URLs (`//cdn.example.com/x.png`) as root-relative and rewrites them to `http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png`, breaking images and links.

### The Problem
```ruby
if href.present? && href.start_with?('/')
  a['href'] = "#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"
```
`'//cdn.example.com/a.png'.start_with?('/')` is true. `sub(/^\/+/, '')` then strips both slashes, so the result is `http://blog.example.com/cdn.example.com/a.png`. The same logic applies to `img[src]` at line 73.

### Theory / Proof
RFC 3986 section 4.2 defines a reference that starts with `//` as a network-path reference: it keeps the host part and inherits only the scheme. Browsers resolve `//cdn.example.com/a.png` against the page's scheme. They never treat it as a path on the current host.

### What happens today vs. what will break
Root-relative links (`/hello`) work, and the spec covers them. Protocol-relative `src`/`href` values are common in blog HTML (CDN images, embedded media), and all of them come out as 404s on the embedding host.

### Research
Ruby's stdlib `URI.join(base, ref)` implements RFC 3986 resolution correctly, including network-path and dot-segment references.

### Recommendation
Let URI do the resolution:
```ruby
def self.absolutize_urls(url, contents)
  fragment = Nokogiri::HTML.fragment(contents)
  { 'a' => 'href', 'img' => 'src' }.each do |tag, attr|
    fragment.css(tag).each do |node|
      v = node[attr]
      next if v.blank?
      node[attr] = URI.join(url, v).to_s rescue v
    end
  end
  fragment.to_html
end
```
This also handles `../relative` paths and non-default ports, which the hand-built prefix gets wrong for https-on-80 and http-on-443.
kept.evidence: topic_embed.rb:64-65/70-71: start_with?('/') is true for '//cdn...', and sub(/^\/+/,'') removes both slashes before the host prefix is added. The rewritten HTML is saved as raw/cooked. No spec covers protocol-relative URLs.

kept.claim: For RSS 2.0 items without a `<content>` element, SimpleRSS returns nil for `i.content`, so `nil.scrub` raises and aborts the whole feed import.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] `i.content.scrub` crashes on standard RSS 2.0 feeds that use `<description>`/`<content:encoded>`

**Severity:** MEDIUM — For RSS 2.0 items without a `<content>` element, SimpleRSS returns nil for `i.content`, so `nil.scrub` raises and aborts the whole feed import.

### The Problem
```ruby
content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)
```
SimpleRSS creates an accessor for each tag it finds. `<content>` is an Atom element. RSS 2.0 items carry their body in `<description>` or `<content:encoded>`, and SimpleRSS exposes those as `description` and `content_encoded`. For a normal WordPress/RSS 2.0 feed, `i.content` is `nil`.

### Theory / Proof
RSS 2.0 spec (cyber.harvard.edu/rss/rss.html#hrelementsOfLtitemgt): item elements are title, link, description, author, category, comments, enclosure, guid, pubDate, source. There is no `content` element. Along the same lines, `i.id` (line 33) is Atom-only; the RSS equivalent is `guid`.

### What happens today vs. what will break
Atom feeds work. The setting is documented as "URL of RSS/ATOM feed to import" (`server.en.yml`). For an RSS feed the first item raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'scrub' for nil`. The job has `retry: false`, so it fails every hour and imports nothing. `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline, so the same exception also kills every `retrieve_topic` job before its `fetch_http` fallback can run.

### Research
Feedjira and the feed-normalizer gem both normalize `content || content_encoded || description` for exactly this reason.

### Recommendation
```ruby
rss.items.each do |i|
  url = i.link
  url = i.guid if url.blank? || url !~ /\Ahttps?\:\/\//
  body = i.content || i.content_encoded || i.description
  next if body.blank?
  content = CGI.unescapeHTML(body.scrub)
  TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)
end
```
kept.evidence: poll_feed.rb:35 has no nil guard. A SimpleRSS item returns nil for a missing :content key, and RSS 2.0 uses description/content:encoded. retry: false. TopicRetriever:41-43 calls PollFeed inline, so fetch_http is never reached. The poll_feed specs stub poll_feed.

kept.claim: Anyone can send a request with a forged Referer and a unique embed_url (e.g. varying query string) to make the forum scrape the embeddable host and create a new topic per URL, while also re-running the full feed poll each time; the per-URL throttle does not stop this.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Unauthenticated requests can create unlimited topics and trigger feed polls

**Severity:** MEDIUM — Anyone can send a request with a forged Referer and a unique embed_url (e.g. varying query string) to make the forum scrape the embeddable host and create a new topic per URL, while also re-running the full feed poll each time; the per-URL throttle does not stop this.

### The Problem
```ruby
Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)
```
The only gate is `ensure_embeddable`, which compares `request.referer`'s host with `embeddable_host`. Referer is a client-controlled header, so `curl -e http://blog.example.com/` passes. `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` throttles on the key `"retrieved:#{@embed_url}"`, so `http://blog.example.com/a?1`, `?2`, `?3` ... are each new keys. Each one runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` (a full HTTP fetch and parse of the feed) and then `TopicEmbed.import_remote`. That call does an HTTP GET and creates a topic, keyed by the exact URL, as `embed_by_username`.

### Theory / Proof
TopicEmbed has a unique index on `embed_url`, and URLs that differ only in query string or fragment are different keys. Readability returns roughly the same article for every variant, so each request creates a duplicate topic. Nothing limits requests per client IP.

### What happens today vs. what will break
Normal use (one blog post, one URL) works. A script looping over `?n=1..10000` creates up to 10000 topics. It also makes the Sidekiq workers download the feed 10000 times and the blog page 10000 times.

### Research
Disqus and similar embed systems identify a thread by a canonical identifier and normalize URLs. Rails/Discourse ship `RateLimiter` (used across `lib/`) for per-IP limits.

### Recommendation
Normalize the URL and rate-limit per IP before enqueuing:
```ruby
embed_url = params.require(:embed_url)
uri = URI(embed_url)
embed_url = "#{uri.scheme}://#{uri.host}#{uri.path}" # drop query/fragment
topic_id = TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)
if topic_id
  ...
else
  RateLimiter.new(nil, "embed-retrieve-#{request.remote_ip}", 10, 1.minute).performed!
  Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)
```
Also stop running `PollFeed` inline from `TopicRetriever`. The scheduled job already covers it.
kept.evidence: embed_controller.rb:26: the Referer gate can be spoofed. topic_retriever.rb:15 compares only the host. The throttle key is per exact URL, so query variants bypass it. PollFeed runs inline on each retrieve, then import_remote creates a topic. The unique index covers only the exact URL, and skip_validations disables the duplicate checks.

kept.claim: If the embedded topic's post is trashed, `embed.post` returns nil (Trashable default scope) and `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises, aborting the hourly feed import for all remaining items.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Update path crashes when the embed's post has been deleted

**Severity:** MEDIUM — If the embedded topic's post is trashed, `embed.post` returns nil (Trashable default scope) and `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` raises, aborting the hourly feed import for all remaining items.

### The Problem
```ruby
post = embed.post
if content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1
  revisor = PostRevisor.new(post)
  revisor.revise!(user, ...)
```
`Post` includes `Trashable` (`app/models/post.rb:16`), and its default scope (`lib/trashable.rb:5`) hides rows where `deleted_at` is set. Once a moderator deletes an imported topic, `embed.post` is `nil`. `PostRevisor#should_revise?` then calls `@post.raw` on nil.

### Theory / Proof
The `TopicEmbed` row is not removed when the post is trashed, and nothing checks for nil here. `PollFeed` iterates over every feed item inside a single `each` with no rescue, so one crash stops processing of the rest of the feed.

### What happens today vs. what will break
The code works until a moderator deletes an imported topic and the source article is edited later (so its sha1 changes). From then on, every hourly poll raises at that item. Items after it in the feed are never imported or updated.

### Research
Discourse elsewhere guards associations to trashable records with `.with_deleted` or by returning early on nil, for example in `PostAction`.

### Recommendation
```ruby
post = embed.post
return nil if post.blank? # topic was deleted by staff, respect that
if content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1
  PostRevisor.new(post).revise!(user, absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, bypass_rate_limiter: true)
  embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)
end
```
kept.evidence: post.rb:16 includes Trashable (default scope hides trashed rows). PostDestroyer trashes the post but leaves the TopicEmbed. topic_embed.rb:32-37 has no nil check, so post_revisor.rb:26 calls @post.raw on nil. poll_feed's each loop has no rescue.

kept.claim: The Disqus importer now fetches every thread's page over HTTP; any 404/timeout raises from open-uri and aborts the whole import, and the `--category` option and original `created_at` were silently removed.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Disqus import regresses: no error handling for remote fetch, category and created_at dropped

**Severity:** MEDIUM — The Disqus importer now fetches every thread's page over HTTP; any 404/timeout raises from open-uri and aborts the whole import, and the `--category` option and original `created_at` were silently removed.

### The Problem
```ruby
post = TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])
```
`import_remote` calls `open(url).read` (`topic_embed.rb:48`) with no rescue. `OpenURI::HTTPError` (404/410 on old Disqus threads is common), `SocketError`, and `Timeout::Error` propagate out of the `parser.threads.each` loop. Separately, the diff removes `method_option :category` and stops passing `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])`.

### Theory / Proof
Disqus exports often contain threads whose pages have since moved or been deleted. Previously the importer needed no network access at all. Now one dead link stops the run partway through, and a re-run duplicates nothing only because the embed_url is unique. All imported topics also carry the import time as their date instead of the original date, and existing scripts that pass `-c` now fail with an unknown-option error.

### What happens today vs. what will break
Small, clean exports work. Real archives with dead links fail partway through, and users who relied on `--category` lose that behaviour without any notice.

### Research
Thor treats unknown options as errors only when `check_unknown_options!` is set; otherwise they are ignored silently. Either way the behaviour change is undocumented.

### Recommendation
```ruby
post = begin
  TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])
rescue OpenURI::HTTPError, SocketError, Timeout::Error => e
  puts "  failed to fetch #{t[:link]}: #{e.message}"
  nil
end
```
Keep the `--category` option and pass `category:` / `created_at:` through `TopicEmbed.import` to `PostCreator`.
kept.evidence: disqus.thor has no rescue, and import_remote calls open(url).read unguarded, so a dead link ends the import. The --category option and created_at are removed, and TopicEmbed.import passes only title/raw. Minor: Thor probably ignores -c silently rather than raising an error.

kept.claim: `setnx` followed by a separate `expire` is not atomic; if the process dies between the two calls the key never expires and that URL is permanently throttled for non-staff.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Non-atomic SETNX + EXPIRE can leave a throttle key without TTL

**Severity:** LOW — `setnx` followed by a separate `expire` is not atomic; if the process dies between the two calls the key never expires and that URL is permanently throttled for non-staff.

### The Problem
```ruby
if $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")
  $redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)
```

### Theory / Proof
Redis documents this pattern as unsafe. SETNX and EXPIRE are two round trips. A crash, Sidekiq shutdown, or network error between them leaves a key with no TTL. Redis 2.6.12+ supports `SET key value NX EX 60`, which does both atomically (redis.io/commands/set, and the SETNX page's note on locking).

### What happens today vs. what will break
Usually both calls succeed. On a worker kill at the wrong moment, that URL never gets retrieved again for anonymous/regular users until someone deletes the key by hand.

### Research
redis-rb supports `redis.set(key, val, nx: true, ex: 60)`.

### Recommendation
```ruby
return false if $redis.set(retrieved_key, "1", nx: true, ex: 60)
true
```
kept.evidence: topic_retriever.rb:27-28 makes separate SETNX and EXPIRE calls. A crash between them leaves the key with no TTL, and no code resets it. The window is tiny, so LOW.

kept.claim: The origin check uses substring matching, so an origin that is a prefix of discourseUrl (e.g. `https://forum.example.co` vs `https://forum.example.com/`) is accepted.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] postMessage origin check uses `indexOf` substring match

**Severity:** LOW — The origin check uses substring matching, so an origin that is a prefix of discourseUrl (e.g. `https://forum.example.co` vs `https://forum.example.com/`) is accepted.

### The Problem
```js
if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }
```
If `discourseUrl` is `https://forum.example.com/`, a message from origin `https://forum.example.co` (a different registrable domain) passes, because `"https://forum.example.com/".indexOf("https://forum.example.co") === 0`.

### Theory / Proof
MDN, Window.postMessage security concerns: "Always verify the sender's identity using the origin... an exact match". A substring check is the classic mistake it warns about.

### What happens today vs. what will break
The impact today is limited: the handler only sets the iframe height. The listener is a trust boundary, though, and any future message type added to this handler inherits the weak check.

### Research
The HTML spec defines origin as an exact scheme://host:port tuple, and the recommended check is strict equality.

### Recommendation
```js
var a = document.createElement('a'); a.href = discourseUrl;
var expectedOrigin = a.protocol + '//' + a.host;
if (e.origin !== expectedOrigin) { return; }
```
kept.evidence: embed.js:17 uses an indexOf substring test, so an origin that is a prefix of discourseUrl passes. The impact is small: the handler only resizes the iframe.

kept.claim: `<%- end if %>` makes the next ERB buffer append the `if` modifier's condition, so the conditional only works by accident.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Stray `if` after `end` in the template

**Severity:** LOW — `<%- end if %>` makes the next ERB buffer append the `if` modifier's condition, so the conditional only works by accident.

### The Problem
```erb
<%- end if %>
```
ERB compiles this to `end if` followed by the next generated statement (the `@output_buffer.safe_append=` for the following text), which Ruby parses as the modifier condition: `(if ... else ... end) if @output_buffer.safe_append=(...)`.

### Theory / Proof
The append returns the buffer, which is truthy, so the block still runs. Its output order is swapped with the whitespace/next chunk, though, and if the next thing were an expression that returns nil/false, the whole header block would silently disappear.

### What happens today vs. what will break
The template renders now because the following chunk is a truthy buffer append. A change such as moving a `<% %>` statement that returns nil to the next line would suppress the header.

### Research
Standard ERB: `<% end %>`.

### Recommendation
```erb
<%- end %>
```
kept.evidence: Erubis 2.7.0 compiles `end if` followed by a newline and the next safe_append, so Ruby parses that append as the modifier condition. It works only because the append is truthy.

kept.claim: `discourse_expires_in` also caches the 'Loading Discussion...' page in the anonymous cache, which is keyed on host+URI and served before the controller, so readers can see a stale loading page for up to a minute after the topic exists.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Loading page is cached by the anonymous cache

**Severity:** LOW — the discussion appears up to about 60s late for anonymous readers, and `ensure_embeddable` is skipped for cached hits

### The Problem
```ruby
discourse_expires_in 1.minute
```
This line runs after both branches, so it also caches `render 'loading'`. `ApplicationController#discourse_expires_in` calls `Middleware::AnonymousCache.anon_cache`, which is keyed on `"ANON_CACHE_#{HTTP_HOST}#{REQUEST_URI}"` (`lib/middleware/anonymous_cache.rb:14`). The middleware is inserted at position 0 and returns cached bodies before the controller runs.

### Theory / Proof
The first anonymous request for a new `embed_url` enqueues `retrieve_topic` and caches the loading page for 60 seconds. `loading.html.erb` reloads itself every 30 seconds. Those reloads hit the same cache key, so they get the cached loading page even after the job has created the topic. Cached hits also skip `before_filter :ensure_embeddable`, so the Referer check is not applied to them. That has little security impact, because the header can be spoofed anyway and the content is public.

### What happens today vs. what will break
This applies only in production (or wherever rack-cache is enabled) and to anonymous GET requests. Readers of a newly embedded article see "Loading Discussion..." for up to a minute longer than necessary. It is also a small waste: the anonymous cache holds a transient page.

### Research
HTTP caching guidance (RFC 7234) is to avoid caching interim or placeholder responses, or to mark them `no-store`. Discourse's anonymous cache has no `Vary` support, so the endpoint cannot cache per Referer either.

### Recommendation
Cache only the rendered discussion:
```ruby
if topic_id
  @topic_view = TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})
  discourse_expires_in 1.minute
else
  Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)
  render 'loading'
end
```
kept.evidence: anonymous_cache.rb:14 keys on host+URI only and serves before the controller, so ensure_embeddable is skipped for cached hits. This applies only in production and for anonymous GETs. The Referer gate can be spoofed anyway and the content is public, and the cached targetOrigin is the same origin for legitimate embedders. The loading page is also cached, which delays the discussion appearing.
kept.corrected_claim: Anon cache (host+URI key, served pre-controller) skips the Referer check for cached hits and caches the loading page, delaying the discussion by up to about a minute. Low practical impact.
